NEWS




Hi folks. This game has been produced and has arrived and is ready to ship.
I know this contest focuses on Print and Play games, but if anyone is interested in buying a copy for themselves, as a gift, or just to help fund the planting of a tree (yes, each game we manufacture funds the planting of one tree), please visit https://www.ex1st.com/games/bananaboy/ where you will find a link to the webstore.

AND if you let me know that you have ordered (by commenting on the WIP thread as soon as you do), I will add an extra copy of the game for free. It's time to celebrate a new game!

If you are looking for a fun present to give to your fun non-gamer friends, give these a try. The will arrive before December, way before you get too busy to get any shopping done, run out of gift ideas, and spiral into madness. The cards, box, and rules are linen finish and very vibrant. It's a super fun game, too.

Thank you for supporting indie publishers!

Hey everyone! I know I'm a few days late but we're in the official playtesting stage of the contest.  So please go in and start playing some games and thinking about which ones are your favorites! I'll get the voting page set up on (or around) 1 November so folks can go in and make their picks when they're ready. Voting will close on 30 November and we'll announce the winners shortly after.

I know we (Side Room Games) are going to start going in and checking out all of the games soon & I'm excited to see what the designers came up with!

Hey everyone! I just got the results posted for both the voting results as well as our jury prize selections! Congrats to all of the folks who placed and congrats to everyone in general for getting their designs in the contest - hopefully the best reward is to see that an initial idea can become a fully fleshed out game!

I just sent out all of the geekgold prizes to folks as well as reached out to our jury prize winners. If you have any questions or issues please feel free to reach out.

Thanks again to everyone! And be on the lookout for a discussion thread for the 2025 9-card contest coming soon - the contest will kick off on 1 January!

At the risk of being massively late: Congrats to the winners, and massive thanks as always to Dustin and team for hosting!

Thanks also to those who played my game, in particular our honorable winners Jeff and Rylie whose thorough review gave me the push I needed!

Glad to see that some more complex games also made the roster this time. I found Alessio's approach to reducing a Pax game to 54 cards particularly encouraging!

Needless but not pointless to say that I am course humbled yet again to find my game among the honorable mentions!

Fun as always! See you later this year for the next iteration!
